question: How can inference operate if perception is ultimately absent?
premises: In ultimate reality there is only one cognition.
Inference is commonly thought to depend on prior perception.
An objection arises about inference in the absence of perception.
inference: The verse raises the problem of how inference is possible if only one ultimate cognition exists.
plain_english: But in reality there is only one ultimate cognition. Yet one may object: how could inference exist in the absence of perception, since it depends on it?
